brief: SocGen's week-ahead note argues growth has proved more resilient than expected and should hold into year-end before moderating in 2027, while sticky energy and food prices, tariffs and firm demand slow disinflation and tilt inflation risk upward, pushing SocGen to expect more central bank tightening almost across the board though the Fed and ECB may stay insufficiently restrictive. In the US, firm August CPI and PPI, hawkish Fed communication (Warsh, Hammack, Musalem) against Waller's conditional dovishness, and trend PCE near 2.5-3% support SocGen's call for a 25bp September hike, with the SEP dots seen showing two 2026 hikes and a 2027 hold. In Europe, oil, gas and electricity prices up over 20% in two weeks drove the ECB to hike and signal more tightening despite growth risk; SocGen sees the next ECB hike in December, not October, and expects the BoE to hold at 3.75%. The BoJ is expected to hike 25bp to 1.25%, with quarterly hikes toward a 2% terminal contingent on the yen and board appointments. Taiwan's CBC is expected to start hiking a quarter early; Brazil's BCB is expected to cut once more to 13.75% before pausing.
